chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) he said: Muhammad ibn Hammam narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Rabah, who said: My uncle Abu al-Qasim Ali ibn Muhammad narrated to me from Ubayd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Khalid al-Tamimi, who narrated to me from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Kazzaz, from his uncle Ya'qub ibn Ilyas, from Mubarak al-Kabbaz, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me:

"Saddle the she-camel and the donkey, for it is time of his arrival, and he is in al-Hirah." He said: So he mounted, and I mounted with him until he entered al-Jurf. Then he dismounted and prayed two rak'ahs. Then he advanced a little further and prayed two rak'ahs. Then he advanced a little further and prayed two rak'ahs. Then he mounted and returned. I said to him: "May I be your ransom, what are the first two, the second two, and the third two?" He said: "The first two rak'ahs are at the place of the grave of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him); the second two rak'ahs are at the place of the head of al-Husayn (peace be upon him); and the third two rak'ahs are at the place of the pulpit of the Qa'im (peace be upon him)."

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤَمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful, a title referring to Imam Ali (peace be upon him).
key_terms.الْجُرْف: Al-Jurf, a specific area or district within al-Hirah.
key_terms.الْحِيرَة: Al-Hirah, a historical city in Iraq near Kufa.
key_terms.الْقَائِم: The Qa'im, referring to the Twelfth Imam, Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (peace be upon him).
key_terms.رَأْسُ الْحُسَيْنِ: The head of Imam Husayn (peace be upon him), referring to his shrine or burial place.
key_terms.رَكْعَتَيْنِ: Two rak'ahs, a unit of prayer consisting of two cycles.

ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual significances of the three locations visited by Imam al-Sadiq in al-Hirah?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) demonstrates the spiritual significance of al-Hirah by performing three distinct sets of two-rak'ah prayers, linking each to a pivotal figure in Shia eschatology and history. The first set honors the grave of Amir al-Mu'minin (AS), the second commemorates the head of Imam Husayn (AS), and the third anticipates the pulpit of the Awaited Imam (al-Qa'im), thereby connecting the Imams of the past with the future Mahdi. This practice underscores the Shia tradition of visiting sacred sites (ziyarat) as a means of drawing closer to the Ahl al-Bayt and affirming the continuity of their leadership.
